To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the seven year mortality rate for patients treated with electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) for depression was 18% (95% confidence interval (CI): 14-22%), and that 40% of patients had been readmitted to hospital at least once during the seven year follow-up period.

(1) The use of ECT is increasing in the United States and is more likely to be prescribed by psychiatrists and general practitioners than by other physicians, (2) ECT use is associated with a lower risk of death and a lower risk of hospital readmission for suicide, and (3) The use of antidepressants, mood stabilizers, and antipsychotics is associated with a higher risk of death and hospital readmission for suicidal behavior.
